newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP Whyalla steel workers strike for day.
newsitem.headline: BHP Whyalla steel workers strike for day.

text.p: Steel production at BHP Pty Co Ltd's Whyalla operation in South Australia had been closed down for 24 hours with up to 1,800 workers on strike to protest likely future job losses, the Australian Workers Union (AWU) said on Wednesday.

AWU branch secretary Geoff Buckland told Reuters steel production and nearby iron ore mining operations would be halted until the first shift on Thursday morning, although a skeleton staff would maintain plant safety.

Buckland said workers at the Whyalla plant, which produced around 280,000 tonnes of steel in the February quarter, earlier had elected not to join a national strike called last week to protest the company's plans to end steel-making at Newcastle, believing they would be quarantined from job losses.
However, he said discussions with management over restructuring plans had revealed future job losses and reductions in take-home pay, through cuts in the number of shifts.
"We are talking pretty serious numbers (of job losses)," he said.

"The action today is not only directed at BHP but certainly at the federal and state governments because we believe they have to take a greater role in securing steelmaking as a vital industry for Australia," he said.
Buckland said there were no plans for any further stoppages.
BHP shares were 17 cents lower at A$19.09 at 12.00 p.m. (0200 GMT) on Wednesday.
